additional_info.subject: Issue reported from the customer (Note for NOC)
additional_info.body:
on Friday, the BS-LT 2306 started charging at 17:21 at 28% and stopped at 19:38 at 55%.
On Saturday, the truck was then connected again and then charged to 100% from 12:45 p.m. at 48% to 2:33 p.m.
Is there a logical explanation for the abandonment on Friday?

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0402658-DC/Si-D/DE-[Y2/S5 313651774001]-charging process was aborted CRM:00641000989
additional_info.body:
Dear Mr. Benjamin Narten,
I hope this message finds you well.
Regarding the reported issue, we have analyzed the logs and found the following:
On
Saturday
, the truck was connected again and successfully charged to 100% from
12:45 PM (48%) to 2:33 PM
.
However, during the session on
Friday
, the charging process was aborted due to the following error:
2025-01-24T18:38:09.984388+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:err] sicharge-cp-backend/361cb2aa0ef4[706]: PLC-Error-Flag 'SECC_DC2_MB_Problem_KF11' changed to true - (loss of communication DC2 and SECC)
2025-01-24T18:38:09.825602+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] [ONR] DC2 : Outlet not ready - SECC has communication error with PLC
2025-01-24T18:38:06.783827+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] [MBC] SECC: no comm for 750ms "DC2"
This error indicates a loss of communication between the SECC and PLC, which could be caused by network outages, server failures, or hardware malfunctions. As a result, the session on Friday was aborted.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: AW: ID0402658-DC/Si-D/DE-[Y2/S5 313651774001]-charging process was aborted CRM:00641000989
additional_info.body:
Dear Mr. Benjamin,
I hope this email finds you well.
Thank you for the information provided so far.
Upon analyzing the logs for this instance, we noticed the following behavior:
When the first vehicle was connected, the charger assigned 75 kW to this outlet based on the smart charging profile split.
However, when a second EV was connected to the other outlet, the power allocation suddenly dropped to ~37 kW.
We suspect that another charger assigned within the same group might have been delivering power to the EV.
To confirm this and proceed with a more thorough analysis, it would be greatly helpful if you could share the serial number of the second charger being used for the same smart charging profile.
In the meantime, we will continue to review the logs for the charger.
Looking forward to your response.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team - Abhinav Malokar

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: AW: AW: ID0402658-DC/Si-D/DE-[Y2/S5 313651774001]-charging process was aborted CRM:00641000989
additional_info.body:
Dear Benjamin,
Hope you are doing well,
Upon reviewing the configuration and logs for the mentioned time 2025-01-24T16:22:01, we could see a charging session was initiated at outlet 2 i.e. DC2. Before I explain the charging logs, let me share some information about the charger configuration and power limit.
Charger is equipped with 4 DC outlets with Maximum power of 300kW, however Charger has an input power limit of 150kVA.
Charger is connected to Depotfinity via OCPP
Depotfinity has smart charging active.
Now, about the charging session:
Session Start
2025-01-24T16:19:52.290247+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] [DCC] DC2: PilotState "A" --> "B2"
Power Limit via OCPP SmartCharging for 0 W
connectorId":1,"csChargingProfiles":{"chargingProfileId":1,"stackLevel":1,"chargingProfilePurpose":"TxProfile","chargingProfileKind":"Relative","chargingSchedule":{"chargingRateUnit":"W","chargingSchedulePeriod":[{"startPeriod":0,"limit":75000}]},"transactionId":396709136}}
hence no energy delivered to Truck
2025-01-24T16:22:01.933602+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] |2025-01-24T16:21:21|DC2|EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=0|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=0|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=0|EVSE_NowCur[A]=0|EVSE_NowVol[V]=644|EV_TarCur[A]=0|EV_TarVol[V]=665|EV_SOC[%]=28|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=248|Pilot=4
Power Limit via OCPP SmartCharging increased to for 36363W i.e. 36.363 kW
2025-01-24T16:22:15.882064+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/361cb2aa0ef4[706]: OCPP: Received command: SetChargingProfile (b9ed578e-e9e2-49b4-a2f8-98d699eb9300) - {"connectorId":1,"csChargingProfiles":{"chargingProfileId":1,"stackLevel":1,"chargingProfilePurpose":"TxProfile","chargingProfileKind":"Relative","chargingSchedule":{"chargingRateUnit":"W","chargingSchedulePeriod":[{"startPeriod":0,"limit":38176}]},"transactionId":396709136}
Charging phase
2025-01-24T16:22:21.933251+00:00 swcpu [user:debug] |2025-01-24T16:21:21|DC2|EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=38|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=58|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=37.6|EVSE_NowCur[A]=58|EVSE_NowVol[V]=646|EV_TarCur[A]=58|EV_TarVol[V]=665|EV_SOC[%]=28|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=248|Pilot=4
Throughout the session was power on Connector 1 was set to 36.36kW, because there were ongoing sessions on Connector 1 of charger 1 & Connector 1&2 of charger second which was part of smart charging profile
And if you add the total power of connector 1, 2 of charger first and
connector 1, 2 of charger second i.e.
37.6kW+37.6KW+37.6KW +37.6KW
it is near equal to 150kW,
which is equivalent to the input power limit of charger.
I have added the relevant logs for your reference, hope this clarifies your doubt.
If you are satisfied with the response and explanation and do not have further question, may I have your acknowledgement to close this case.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Abhinav
